## Design

### 2026-10-25 – I've spent a lot of time researching how MIDI controllers work and the best way to assemble them. I was thinking of using perf board for my project but because the cherry MX switches are a weird dimen

**2h**

I've spent a lot of time researching how MIDI controllers work and the best way to assemble them. I was thinking of using perf board for my project but because the cherry MX switches are a weird dimension I am switching to making a custom PCB.

I am going to start with just 1 board with 10 total keys because that is a nice number for most packages. Or I might do 12 if I can find some for cheap.

I plan to have the main keys be a separate board from the ESP32 which will be in charge of sending MIDI signals to my computer to be processed. This way I can always add more keys later.

The keys will be laid out in a matrix so I can use less GIOP pins. There will be a diode for each switch to prevent ghosting.

Tomorrow is the last day this week and I will have to spend a lot of time finalizing things because I have been busy with real life stuff this week. I still need to decide if I want to add LEDs in or just keep it simpler.

### 2026-10-25 – Today I finished my project. I finalized the wiring and routed the PCB. Because this is my second time, it only took 2 hours to get the PCB in a place that I liked. I did research on other MIDI contro

**4h**

Today I finished my project. I finalized the wiring and routed the PCB. Because this is my second time, it only took 2 hours to get the PCB in a place that I liked. I did research on other MIDI controllers and macro pads. In the future I would like to design a case for this but right now it will just be a PCB with key switches on it.

My plan for running the MIDI code is using an ESP32 dev board and then connecting it to my  computer to run the music program. I added a 7 pin connector the the PCB that I will just jumper wires to connect to my ESP32 so that I can easily adapt to whatever board or configuration I end up going with.

I found switches and key caps for a reasonable price online and found diodes for the matrix. I will be ordering the PCB from JLCPCB.

I also spent time researching how to use the signals from the macropad to control a music program but I haven't finalized the code yet. I will work more on it during the build week once I can have a physical interface to test with.
